guidelines.detail: refines ACT-02 (The description says the parts are assembled and inspected manually with no software mentioned, but the generated model uses a serviceTask for assembly. ACT-03 reserves serviceTask for automated work, so the element type was misapplied. The reference's userTask for inspection conflicts with ACT-02 and is not used as the basis for this guideline. same as LRN-003 (The reference has parallel gateways ParallelGateway_1 and ParallelGateway_2 around the parallel ordering task (M9, M10), and the description says the ordering is carried out in parallel (S3). The generated model has neither gateway, so the parallel work is not opened and closed by a fork and join. The guideline states this structural pattern for a single parallel activity.)

new guideline (The generated model uses the start event "Chainsaw properties received" (X1) where the reference has a separate step for determining the properties (M1). The description says the customer told the properties and the producer then orders parts (S2, S3), so the receipt and the work on it are two distinct things. rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description joins two activities with 'and' (for example, one party performs both actions for the same case) and gives no stated order between them, so both must be completed before the flow continues: Model the two activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before them and a parallel gateway join after them, so the next step starts only when both branches have completed. Do not model them as a sequence with an arbitrary order, and do not model them as alternatives.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that, after a preceding step, one activity is carried out in parallel for several items (for example, marked with an explicit '(in parallel)' note), and a later step depends on all of those items being obtained

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a step is carried out by people physically handling items (for example assembling or inspecting them) and names no software or system that performs or supports the work: Model that step as a bpmn:manualTask, not as a bpmn:serviceTask (which is reserved for automated service work) or a bpmn:userTask (which requires software assistance). Keep the step as a separate activity when the description describes it separately.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an external party (such as a customer) has provided information, and the producer then performs a distinct step that works on that information (for example determining, specifying or preparing items from it): Model the arrival of the information as an event (a message start event or an intermediate catch event, as the description implies), and keep the producer's subsequent step as its own activity placed after that event. Use a userTask or manualTask according to whether the description states software support. Do not let the receipt event replace the step that works on the information.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a group of activities may be carried out in parallel, starting from one point and leading to a later step that needs all of them finished: Open the group of parallel activities with a parallel gateway split placed after the point where they may start, give each activity its own outgoing branch from that split, and close the branches with a parallel gateway join before the later step. Do not sequence the activities one after another, and do not add decision conditions to these branches.
